newsitem.title: THAILAND: ASEAN ministers to meet Ranariddh in Bangkok.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN ministers to meet Ranariddh in Bangkok.

text.p: Three Southeast Asian foreign ministers will meet ousted Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh in Bangkok on Friday, Thailand's Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn said on Thursday.

He said that his counterparts from Indonesia and the Philippines would join him in the meeting with Ranariddh to try to solve the problems in Cambodia after the prince was deposed by powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen earlier this month.

Ranariddh, who has been lobbying for international support since his ouster, would arrive in Bangkok from Rome on Friday morning and later in the day meet Prachuab, Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas and Domingo Siazon of the Philippines.

The meeting is mandated by the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) and aimed at resolving conflicts between the two Cambodian leaders. The ministers would then travel to Phnom Penh on Saturday to meet Hun Sen, Prachuab said in a teleconference from Beijing.
"ASEAN wants to promote independence and does not wish to see any conflict in Cambodia. We do not wish to see any cold war just like in the 1980s in Cambodia," he added.

Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot, a senior member of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, on Wednesday was chosen by the remnants of the royalist party to succeed Ranariddh, prompting condemnation from the United States.
